skill.name: Implement
skill.prompt:
## Implementation

Implement the current Goal Round using all accepted plans and attached Skills. Inspect existing code, make the complete change, run appropriate verification, and report evidence for each checklist item. Check the plan's assumptions against the code and keep policy in its shared owner. Prefer one correction that explains the affected behavior over separate fixes at each failing call site. Report evidence-backed plan deviations within the Goal's scope and existing authority. Preserve unrelated changes and historical evidence.

### Intent and architecture

Review Refine's relevant documentation files under Refine's runtime at `<refine-runtime>/docs/intent/***/*.*` as the durable product specification.

### Semantic code organization

Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.

current_round.prompt: For the web UI surface, create two new main nav right-aligned dropdown buttons, one for Skills and one for Sites. The right-aligned button order should be Skills, Sites, Settings, and New Goal. Yes, that is a rename of Controls to Settings. Move the menus from Settings (formerly Controls) to the appropriate new menu for Sites and Skills. Add a separator to the new menus for New Skill, New Site, Manage Skills, and Manage Sites. Ensure you use the standardized styles and layout we already have in the app.

agent_context.workflow_summary: Refine gives this Goal Agent an isolated worktree and a finalized implementation plan. Implement the current Round and report evidence; a separate agent will review and correct the candidate in Quality, then an independent Governance gate will verify policy and integrate the exact passing commit before human Review. Do not directly advance Goal state, approve, merge, or push.

checklist.description: Establish the navigation contract: the cause is that independent Skill and Site entry points are grouped inside Controls. The browser shell owns their placement and shared dropdown behavior; settings_skills.js and knowledge-hub.js already own their lists and actions. Preserve those owners and existing application capabilities. Update the checkout's navigation, Skills, and Knowledge Hub intent docs to describe the requested arrangement.

Update src/surfaces/web/static/index.html so the right-aligned actions appear in order: Skills, Sites, Settings, New Goal. Move the existing Skill and Site containers into their respective dropdowns. Rename the Controls button and accessible label to Settings. Reuse shared summary, panel, icon, and menu-row styles from css/base.css; preserve the remaining settings controls and New Goal's related creation actions.

Update settings_skills.js and knowledge-hub.js to show existing entries followed by a separator and an action group: New Skill then Manage Skills, or New Site then Manage Sites. New actions open the existing creation modals; management links navigate to #/settings/skills and #/settings/knowledge-hub. Keep these actions available with empty lists, and render list failures separately from the action group. Preserve Skill eligibility, input preflight, agent-tab launch, and Site draft/published URL handling.

Bind each list's refresh-on-open listener to its new dropdown while retaining existing load, definition-change, and node-context refresh behavior and stale-response guards. Use common.js's shared topbar menu handling for mutual exclusion, action dismissal, outside clicks, and Escape. Extend shared selectors only where needed. Use shared border and spacing tokens for separators, and verify panels remain usable with long lists and narrow viewports.

Update user-facing navigation references in Guide, Skill help, reporter onboarding, and toolbar Todo copy to the new locations. Preserve existing route and element identities where practical, including Node and Reporter selectors, so the label change does not break shell integrations.

Update src/surfaces/web_server/tests/static_surface/navigation.rs and add focused browser coverage for action order, exclusive list placement, separators, all four create/manage actions, empty and failed lists, refresh after node or definition changes, Skill launch, and Site opening. Exercise keyboard operation, dismissal, light/dark themes, and desktop/narrow layouts. Proposed checks on the implementation derived from pinned base 9c1be94cf6421854a1c6693b7403b57d8f7576b2: cargo run --manifest-path xtask/Cargo.toml -- test-unit; node --test tests/web_topbar_navigation.test.js tests/web_knowledge_hub.test.js tests/web_node_scope_navigation.test.js tests/web_reporter_onboarding.test.js tests/web_theme.test.js. Require browser cases to execute rather than skip, and report failures separately from verified results.

checklist.evidence: Reviewed and updated navigation, Skills, and Knowledge Hub intent docs. Preserved shell ownership of navigation and existing capability owners.
Actions now appear as Skills, Sites, Settings, New Goal. Browser and Rust assertions verify order and exclusive list placement; existing Settings controls and creation routes remain.
Both lists have separators followed by New and Manage actions. Browser checks verify all four actions, empty/failed lists, Skill eligibility and typed launch, and draft/published Site opening.

Refresh-on-open targets the new menus. Added missing Hub node-change and mutation refresh hooks and guarded stale failures. Shared dismissal handles all panels. Chromium verified keyboard opening, Escape, outside clicks, mutual exclusion, and long lists at 1440, 800, and 375 pixels in both themes.
Updated Guide, Skill help, reporter onboarding, and Todo copy. Preserved Node, Reporter, context-menu, and route identities. Existing onboarding and managed-terminal Skill browser tests pass.
Focused JavaScript and static-surface checks pass without browser skips. Full Rust verification exposed seven unresolved failures outside this change; logs preserve exact identities and diagnostics.
